guards.instead: Write the token as a whole JSON string, "[#NAME:key#]", to get a number, or use [$NAME:key$] inside a longer string.
guards.why: The initializer only replaces [#…#] when the double quotes are part of the delimiter. Anywhere else it stays literal and resolves to nothing.

guards.instead: Use ObjectField_<fieldName>, or [$OBJECT_FIELD_KEY:<Object>:<field>#<subfield>$] for an attachment subfield (resolved by masterclass-cms-workarounds).
guards.why: A numeric object field ID was captured from the instance the page was authored on, and matches nothing on any other instance. The attachment mappings broke this way (rlluis/devcon2026#39).

guards.instead: Use the relationship's declared name from object-relationships/ or the batch.
guards.why: A relationship name of the form name<hex> was generated by the authoring instance, so a collection provider naming it resolves nowhere else.

guards.instead: Use "scope": "1" (company) or "2" (site) for a grant on existing entries.
guards.why: Scope 3 only sets default permissions for entries created later. It applies without an error and changes nothing for entries that already exist.

guards.instead: Leave system out, or set it to false.
guards.why: Copied from a portal initializer, "system": true makes the object or picklist unmodifiable.

guards.instead: Import or link .agents/liferay-rules.md (GEMINI.md uses @.agents/liferay-rules.md; .claude/CLAUDE.md is a symlink) and list only agent-specific additions.
guards.why: A copied skill router drifts. .gemini/GEMINI.md had fallen behind .agents/liferay-rules.md, and Gemini never read it anyway.
